blocks.prompt: 11. If \(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}\) and \(\frac{1}{c}\) are in G.P. Show that the common ratio is \(\pm\sqrt{\frac{a}{c}}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh proof wala sawal hai: teen numbers ke ulte (reciprocals) G.P. mein hain.
Diya kya hai? \(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}, \frac{1}{c}\) G.P. mein hain.
Saabit kya karna hai? Common ratio \(\pm\sqrt{a/c}\) hai.
Plan: G.P. ki sharait se \(b^2 = ac\) nikalenge, phir ratio \(\frac{a}{b}\) ka square le kar \(b^2\) ki jagah \(ac\) rakhenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}, \frac{1}{c}\) G.P. mein hain (\(a, b, c\) zero nahi).
Saabit karna hai: common ratio \(= \pm\sqrt{a/c}\).
Tareeqa: Teen terms G.P. mein hon to beech wale ka square = pehla \(\times\) teesra. Yeh rule isi se nikalta hai ke dono ratios barabar hote hain.

G.P. ki sharait lagayein
\[\left(\dfrac{1}{b}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{a} \cdot \dfrac{1}{c}\]
\[\dfrac{1}{b^2} = \dfrac{1}{ac} \Rightarrow b^2 = ac\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1/b}{1/a} = \frac{1/c}{1/b}\) ko cross multiply karein to yahi milta hai. Do fractions jin ke upar 1 ho barabar hon to un ke neeche wale bhi barabar hote hain, is liye \(b^2 = ac\).

Common ratio likhein
\[r = \dfrac{1/b}{1/a} = \dfrac{a}{b}\]
Kyun: Ratio = doosra term \(\div\) pehla term. \(\frac{1}{b} \div \frac{1}{a} = \frac{1}{b} \times \frac{a}{1} = \frac{a}{b}\): fraction se divide karne ka matlab us ke ulte se multiply karna hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{b}{a}\) likh dena (ulta) aam ghalti hai.

Square kar ke \(b^2 = ac\) rakhein
\[r^2 = \dfrac{a^2}{b^2} = \dfrac{a^2}{ac} = \dfrac{a}{c}\]
\[r = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{a}{c}}\]
Kyun: \(r\) mein \(b\) hai jo humein nahi chahiye; square karne se \(b^2\) bana jise \(ac\) se badal sakte hain. Upar neeche ek \(a\) cancel hua. Square root mein \(\pm\) dono aate hain, kyunke \(b\) khud \(\pm\sqrt{ac}\) ho sakta hai; \(r\) ka sign \(a/b\) ke sign jaisa hoga.

Tasdeeq: numbers se
\[\tfrac{1}{a}, \tfrac{1}{b}, \tfrac{1}{c} = 1, 2, 4\]
\[a = 1,\ c = \tfrac{1}{4}:\ \sqrt{a/c} = \sqrt{4} = 2 = r\ \checkmark\]
Kyun: G.P. \(1, 2, 4\) ka ratio 2 hai. Yahan \(a = 1\) aur \(\frac{1}{c} = 4\) yani \(c = \frac{1}{4}\); \(\sqrt{a/c} = 2\) bilkul wohi ratio hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: common ratio \(\pm\sqrt{\frac{a}{c}}\) hai.
